title: Domestication of sorghum in Africa
summary: The eastern Sahel has long been proposed as the most likely centre of sorghum domestication. Seed impressions on Butana Group pottery, from the fourth millennium BC in the southern Atbai region, show cultivated sorghum with some domestic traits. Sorghum was first domesticated in northeast-central Africa, likely 5,000 to 6,000 years ago, and later spread across Africa and into India. It is now the fifth cereal worldwide for grain production and the staple food of around 500 million people.
